topic: Choosing long-term health over short-term pleasure: the effort of training passes quickly but what it builds stays; the comfort we choose instead passes just as fast and leaves nothing behind
figure: Musonius Rufus (saying preserved by Aulus Gellius, Attic Nights 16.1: if you accomplish something noble with toil, the toil passes but the noble deed remains; if something shameful with pleasure, the pleasure passes but the shame remains; Gellius notes Cato the Elder said much the same at Numantia). Paraphrased, not quoted. Single quote page, at Mintra's request
